tactile_skin.note: This is a third-party e-skin build (Shanghai-based JQ Industries' fabric-based piezoresistive tactile sensor, woven with conductive fibers that detect pressure, contact and force distribution), demonstrated on a Unitree G1 chassis as a showcase platform -- not a Unitree-manufactured or Unitree-sold component. A short video of the demo is publicly referenced ('This Robot's Skin Can Actually Feel Touch', YouTube Shorts, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/k9tj5kb3rHI) but could not be directly viewed during this build (YouTube consent redirect blocked automated fetch); 'demonstrated' status rests on the press description of an actual JQ Industries demo rather than direct video verification, and should be revisited if the video can be reviewed frame-by-frame.

source.quote: the default manufacturer-provided recovery controller on the Unitree G1, which executes a hard-coded joint trajectory with PD stabilization

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for the exact recorded robot variant were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: Independent research paper (not Unitree marketing) describes and benchmarks the stock get-up behavior shipped on the robot; it is a fixed, hard-coded trajectory, not a learned or teleoperated one, hence 'scripted' rather than 'autonomous'.

sdk.note: unitree_sdk2 (BSD-3-Clause license per the repo's own license metadata) is Unitree's own published SDK, used by developers to control shipped units. ROS2 support is via the separate unitree_ros2 repository, which ships a G1-specific low-level control example ('g1/lowlevel/g1_low_level_example: Low level control for G1', github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros2, accessed 2026-09-21) built on CycloneDDS, the same transport ROS2 uses -- this is demonstrated, shipped-grade tooling, not a claim.

notes: Height/weight conflict: Unitree's current product page (accessed 2026-09-20) states "1320x450x200mm" and "About 35kg", while The Robot Report's May 2024 launch coverage stated 127 cm and 47 kg for the same base G1. Both are shown here as the current manufacturer figure; the discrepancy is not resolved.
G1 is listed for direct purchase on Unitree's own storefront (checkout, no waitlist), which is strong claimed-level evidence of availability.

Shipped bar: Fraunhofer IPA states it received a Unitree G1 EDU-4 in May 2025 and separately reports campus unboxing. Durham University reports receipt of its G1 Edu “Alan” by 1 April 2026. Both are named external recipients; neither source supports an exact day of first customer delivery. The previous Durham URL was inaccessible; the dur.ac.uk address is accessible.

The 100m obstacle race result is attributed to G1 per Unitree's own social post naming the G1 for this event; the Shanghai Gaoyi Technology government press release (source above) confirms the time and team but does not itself name the robot model, since it covers both the G1 obstacle result and the H1 400m result from the same subsidiary team in one paragraph.

locomotion left out (2026-09-21): searched the manufacturer's own product/press page and its main launch coverage (The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum / named outlet where applicable) for a literal quote naming the propulsion ("bipedal", "legs", "walks", "wheeled base", etc.); none of the pages fetched in this pass contained a checkable sentence naming it specifically for G1 -- most pages describe height/DOF/speed without ever stating the locomotion type in words. Left out rather than inferred from photos or category. Revisit with a source that states it directly.
